reviewer: Codex independent arm A; direct whole saved image and unresampled native crops
review_inputs: original supplied reference viewed directly pre-core

gates.criterion: Primary visible facial proportions/features and chin-length dark bob/wispy fringe resemble the supplied reference within the specified appearance-only scope.
gates.evidence: At native scale, the lead retains a tapered oval face, dark rounded almond eyes, small rounded nose, natural pink lips and a straight dark chin-length bob with wispy forehead strands. Visible guidance is recognizable at the changed pose; this is not an identity judgment.

gates.criterion: The image visibly reads as musicians sharing a working-stage cue and musical action, with guitar and at least two bandmates; decorative instruments alone fail.
gates.evidence: Three distinct musicians occupy a working venue stage: lead electric guitar, bassist and seated drum kit. Lead and bassist hands engage their instruments and drummer holds sticks; reciprocal attention supports shared musical activity rather than prop decoration.

gates.criterion: One lead performer owns both hands, left fingertips contact fretboard strings and right pick contacts strings over pickups; full wrist chains, instrument neck/body and targets are distinguishable together.
gates.evidence: Both wrists/arms belong to the lead. Left fingertips curve onto distinct fretboard string positions; right thumb/index hold a visible yellow pick at the strings above the pickup region. Neck, headstock, body and bridge are present in one frame.

gates.criterion: Lead guitar output plug, continuous visible cable route, and amplifier input plug are all visible together and connected; partial route or implied endpoint fails.
gates.evidence: Output plug and top/front amplifier input plug are visible, but the floor route goes behind/under the lead shoes and overlaps an additional connector/line near the amplifier lower left. A single complete continuously visible route between the specified endpoints cannot be established.

gates.criterion: Lead has both shoes on stage and a readable strap carrying the guitar; drummer seated support is coherent.
gates.evidence: Lead shoes contact the stage and shoulder strap carries the guitar. Drummer knee is visible but stool/seat support is hidden by the kit and amplifier; the complete prospective support relation is not visible together.

gates.criterion: Lead head cue and drummer response/snare contact are connected by attention in one frame rather than isolated poses.
gates.evidence: Lead and drummer look toward one another and the head cue is plausible, but the horizontal stick tip is not visibly contacting the snare head. A still frame also cannot prove a first audible or simultaneous beat; only the directed cue/response posture is supported.

strict_whole_scene.reason: Cable route, drummer support and definitive snare contact do not all survive in one view.

controls_calibration.unlabeled_impression: Warm, attentive, relaxed trio rehearsal with a prominent face and red guitar, softly lit by windows; the interpersonal exchange feels gentle and ordinary.
controls_calibration.perceived_expression: Subtle warmth and unguarded smile are compatible with sensual1; no added fetish or surreal treatment is apparent. Ordinal intensity is a reviewer impression, not a measured score or requester preference.

strengths: The warm window/stage mix and central red guitar produce clear hierarchy and a specific working-band situation.
Eyelines connect the lead and two bandmates and give the photograph social presence.
Primary hands and instrument silhouette remain readable with the supplied appearance guidance.
weaknesses: Technical route/support evidence is weaker than the complete authorial plan.
Still pixels support mutual attention and playing posture more strongly than the story of the very first shared beat.
artistic_review.overall: A convincing warm band-rehearsal photograph, with incomplete strict relation fidelity.

causal_data_improvement: unproven; no candidate-derived effect retained and no paired pre-data render exists
